Setting and displaying the options of the package

Source: R/options.R
options.Rd

** Information on the settings for the delta notation **

Usage

options_IsoriX(...)

getOption_IsoriX(x = NULL)

Arguments

...

A named value or a list of named values. The following values, with their defaults, are used:

title_delta_notation

NULL (default) or a name, call, or expression used in the titles of isoscape plots to refer to the delta notation (see above).

example_maxtime

The number of seconds allowed for a given example to run. It is used to control whether the longer examples should be run or not based on the comparison between this option and the approximate running time of the example on our computers.

Ncpu

An integer (default 2L) corresponding to the number of CPUs to be used by the functions that can handle parallel processing: isomultifit, isomultiscape, getelev and prepraster. Use 1L to prevent parallel processing.

dont_ask

A logical indicating if the user prompt during interactive session during plotting must be inactivated (for development purposes only).

spaMM_blocksize

A positive integer (default 16000L) giving the number of locations per slice used by spaMM to compute the prediction variances in isoscape (argument blockSize of spaMM::predict). Larger values are faster but use more memory; lower it if isoscape runs out of memory on large rasters.

spaMM_debugmod

A logical indicating if the warnings and errors produced by the spaMM package should stopped being turned into messages (for development purposes only).

x

A character string holding an option name.

Value

The options are invisibly returned in an object called IsoriX:::.data_IsoriX$options

Details

By default, the titles of isoscape plots do not mention any isotope since IsoriX cannot know which isotope you are working with (the default value of title_delta_notation is NULL). You can define the delta notation to be used in the titles of all plots by setting this option, e.g. options_IsoriX(title_delta_notation = bquote(delta^2*H)) for hydrogen, or options_IsoriX(title_delta_notation = bquote(delta^18*O)) for oxygen.

If the delta symbol is not rendered on your plots (i.e. the title only shows the superscript and the element), the problem comes from the font used by the graphic device to draw Greek letters, not from IsoriX. This happens for example with CairoPNG() from the package Cairo on some systems. You can then:

  • tell Cairo which font to use for symbols, using a font installed on your system that contains Greek letters, e.g. Cairo::CairoFonts(symbol = "DejaVu Sans", usePUA = FALSE);

  • use another graphic device, e.g. png(type = "cairo");

  • or use the Unicode character for delta, e.g. options_IsoriX(title_delta_notation = bquote(italic("\u03B4")^2*H)). Note that this last solution does not work with the device pdf().

Examples

OldOptions <- options_IsoriX()
OldOptions
#> $title_delta_notation
#> NULL
#> 
#> $example_maxtime
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $Ncpu
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $dont_ask
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $spaMM_blocksize
#> [1] 16000
#> 
#> $spaMM_debug
#> [1] FALSE
#> 

## defining the delta notation used in the titles of isoscape plots,
## e.g. for hydrogen:
options_IsoriX(title_delta_notation = bquote(delta^2*H))
getOption_IsoriX("title_delta_notation")
#> delta^2 * H

## or for oxygen:
options_IsoriX(title_delta_notation = bquote(delta^18*O))
getOption_IsoriX("title_delta_notation")
#> delta^18 * O

getOption_IsoriX("example_maxtime")
#> [1] 5
options_IsoriX(example_maxtime = 30)
options_IsoriX()
#> $title_delta_notation
#> delta^18 * O
#> 
#> $example_maxtime
#> [1] 30
#> 
#> $Ncpu
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $dont_ask
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $spaMM_blocksize
#> [1] 16000
#> 
#> $spaMM_debug
#> [1] FALSE
#> 

## restoring the original options:
options_IsoriX(OldOptions)
options_IsoriX()
#> $title_delta_notation
#> NULL
#> 
#> $example_maxtime
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $Ncpu
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $dont_ask
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $spaMM_blocksize
#> [1] 16000
#> 
#> $spaMM_debug
#> [1] FALSE
#>
